summary: Galois representations attached to regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over CM and totally real fields, planned at target level in ten layers: algebraic weights, Hecke characters and good polynomials (AG2.0); compact unitary PEL geometry, coefficient projectors and raw traces (AG2.1a); the Mantovan comparison, weight separation and actual constituents (AG2.1b); polarization twists, solvable base change and discrete assembly (AG2.2); definite-unitary families and solvable descent to arbitrary regular weight (AG2.3); the HLTT ordinary boundary and nonselfdual existence (AG2.4); local comparison, monodromy and purity away from the coefficient prime (AG2.5); coefficient-prime comparison and compatible families (AG2.6); residual representations, genericity and exports (AG2.7). The specification has 124 targets: 16 nodes here and 108 reused targets of the accepted AG2.0 and AG2.6 parts, whose full contracts are given in importChecks and await installation by the maintainer (gap 18). Every layer is planned, with supplier requests and precise source and proof gaps; nothing is closed or implemented.

nodes.title: Comparison of the early polynomial with normalized local Langlands
nodes.statement: For spherical π_v, after ET.6 fixes geometric Artin and the Harris–Taylor normalization, rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2}) is unramified with Frobenius polynomial equal to the AG2.0 integral Hecke polynomial. Shin and Caraiani write L_n(π_v)=rec(π_v^∨|det|^{(1−n)/2}): the same geometric normalization applied to the contragredient (Shin §2.3, p.10; Caraiani’s published Theorem 1.1, p.1598). Chenevier–Harris record that their ρ_{λ,Π} is Harris–Taylor’s R_ℓ(Π^∨). A source representation R_ℓ(Π) normalized by L_n therefore has the good polynomials of Π^∨, and for conjugate self-dual Π the AG2.0 representation attached to Π is R_ℓ(Π^∨)≅R_ℓ(Π)^c. BLGGT, Chenevier–Harris, HLTT, ACC+ and AHTW use rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2}) without the dual. The square-root Satake extension cancels from the integral coefficients. rec^T is the corresponding arithmetic/rational normalization of the source; geometric-to-arithmetic Frobenius takes the normalized reciprocal polynomial. This is a comparison with the constructed local correspondence, and is not an early prerequisite for raw geometry. The term arithmetic normalization for rec^T in ACC+ does not change its geometric Frobenius convention; inversion of Frobenius is a separate operation.
hypotheses: Use the chosen coefficient embedding and geometric Frobenius on both sides.
Import the exact local reciprocity/Satake normalization from ET.6; do not invert roots in just one side.
proofSteps: Compare ET.6’s unramified local parameter with the normalized Satake character.
Apply the IHG.3 factorization and twist formula.

Compare the source dictionaries: pass from Π to Π^∨≅Π^c for Shin’s and Caraiani’s L_n, use rec^T(π_v)=rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2}) for ACC+ and AHTW, and apply reciprocal conversion for arithmetic Frobenius.
acceptance: Check the n = 1 case: an algebraic Hecke character and the twist |det|^{(1-n)/2} = 1, so the dictionary must reduce to class field theory in the chosen normalization
Check the n = 2 case against the R19 convention (characteristic polynomial X^2 - a_l X + eps(l) l^{k-1} at good arithmetic Frobenius) and record the twist relating the two
For n=1 and a conjugate self-dual character χ, L_1(χ_v)=rec(χ_v^{−1}); a source representation normalized by L_1 is the AG2.0 character of χ^{−1}=χ^c, the conjugate of the AG2.0 character of χ.

sources.match: The normalized good parameter is the one supplied by local Langlands.
This notation refers rec and rec^T to the earlier Clozel–Thorne convention; this page alone does not prove the normalization formula.
Art sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius, while rec^T is called the arithmetic normalization. These two uses of normalization must be distinguished.
Defines L_n by applying rec to the contragredient and twisting by |·|^{−(n−1)/2}; Shin’s R_l is normalized by it.

nodes.title: Arbitrary regular conjugate-self-dual existence
nodes.statement: For any CM F, regular algebraic conjugate-self-dual cuspidal π on GL_n(A_F), prime ℓ and coefficient isomorphism ι, there is a unique-up-to-isomorphism continuous semisimple rank-n r attached at good places. No odd-rank, slight-regularity, finite-place square-integrability, finite-slope, unramified-field or imaginary-quadratic-subfield hypothesis remains. CH Theorem 3.2.3 also proves domination away from ℓ and the de Rham/crystalline/semistable assertions, but those exports are assigned to AG2.5 and AG2.6. For an essentially polarized form apply the algebraic-character twist and undo it.
hypotheses: Regular algebraic cuspidal and conjugate self-dual; n=1 comes from class field theory. The GSp₄ case is assigned to the dedicated proposed owner.
proofSteps: Construct the finite-slope definite-unitary target point from strongly regular classical points.
Remove the field and unramified hypotheses by S-general patching, and remove the Iwahori hypothesis by induction on solvable index.
For essentially polarized pairs, apply the prescribed algebraic polarization twist and recover good-place attachment.
acceptance: An even-rank form whose weight has no strict odd-index gap is included.
Every coefficient prime is included, including those at which the initial eigenvariety point has no finite-slope refinement.

sources.match: Arbitrary regular CSD existence follows from the separate interpolation and patching steps.

nodes.title: HLTT existence over arbitrary CM and totally real fields
nodes.statement: For E totally real or CM and π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_n(A_E), every prime p and coefficient isomorphism ι yield a continuous semisimple rank-n r attached at good places. HLTT Theorem 7.13 constructs it first for F=F₀F⁺ with p split in F₀ and the stated source good primes; Corollary 7.14 removes the auxiliary field restrictions by effective patching and proves unramifiedness and the normalized polynomial at all v|q≠p for rational q where π is unramified above q. No polarization is required; the theorem here asserts neither de Rham admissibility at p nor full monodromy at ramified primes.
hypotheses: Regular algebraic cuspidal; geometric Artin and the common integral polynomial convention; n=1 supplied by the algebraic-character construction.
proofSteps: Apply factor separation on the auxiliary imaginary-quadratic compositum.
Vary linearly disjoint auxiliary CM fields, preserving cuspidality and splitting testing places.
Use effective continuous patching, overlap recognition and good polynomials to descend to E.
acceptance: All coefficient primes occur.
A nonselfdual regular algebraic cuspidal π is included.
Good-place equality is not promoted to ramified monodromy equality.

sources.match: The final auxiliary-field descent supplies the nonselfdual rank-n representation.

nodes.title: Varma’s semisimplified comparison and monodromy bound
nodes.statement: For E totally real or CM and regular algebraic cuspidal π on GL_n(A_E), the constructed r_{p,ι}(π) satisfies WD(r|_{G_{E_v}})^ss≅ι^−1rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2})^ss for every v∤p, and WD(r|_{G_{E_v}})^{F-ss}≺ι^−1rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2}). Extract the local bound from the varying-twist 2n family and then remove the split-place and auxiliary-CM restrictions by the source extension/descent argument. The comparison retains no asserted equality of monodromy for arbitrary nonselfdual π.
hypotheses: Regular algebraic cuspidal; every v∤p; the source parameter convention and the full isotypic dominance relation.
proofSteps: Establish the split-place local Weil traces and nilpotent bound in the 2n ordinary family.
Choose a sufficiently large twist avoiding the finitely many isotypic collisions; extract the rank-n first factor and its local bound as in §10.
Use the auxiliary CM extensions of §11 and effective patching to recover all v∤p.
acceptance: A Steinberg target permits a smaller Galois monodromy under the bound; strictness is not asserted to occur in any actual automorphic example.
Semisimplification equality does not remove N from the meaning of the separate F-ss bound.

sources.locator: Theorem (1), p. 1; Proposition 8.1 and proof, pp. 18–19; Proposition 9.1 and proof, pp. 20–26; Theorem 10.2 and Corollary 10.3, §10, pp. 26–27
sources.match: The completed route gives the semisimple local comparison and the monodromy bound at all away places.

nodes.title: Caraiani’s full away-prime compatibility
nodes.statement: For CM L and regular algebraic CSD cuspidal π on GL_n(A_L), every prime ℓ and every v∤ℓ satisfy WD(r_{ℓ,ι}(π)|_{G_{L_v}})^{F-ss}≅ι^−1rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2}) including N. Choose the source solvable extensions and two-signature tensor-square instance, prove its monodromy purity, descend purity to the rank-n representation, and combine with the semisimple local comparison and temperedness. This is full WD compatibility under the polarized source hypotheses, not a conclusion for arbitrary nonselfdual HLTT systems or for v|ℓ.
hypotheses: Regular algebraic CSD cuspidal; v∤ℓ; source geometric normalization and coefficient embedding.
proofSteps: Choose the source auxiliary extensions and compare the tensor-square geometric constituent.
Use the double weight sequence, tensor-square detection and finite-extension invariance to establish Galois WD purity.
Use tempered automorphic purity and equality of semisimple Weil parts, then pure-extension uniqueness up to equivalence.

Caraiani states Theorem 7.4 for R_l(Π) against L_n(Π_y), which applies rec to the contragredient. Apply it to π^∨≅π^c, again regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual and cuspidal, to obtain the displayed statement for the AG2.0 representation of π.
acceptance: The isomorphism preserves N, not only Frobenius eigenvalues.
The companion coefficient-prime log-crystalline theorem belongs to AG2.6.

sources.match: The tensor-square geometric route proves the full away-prime result.

nodes.title: Comparison strength at the coefficient prime
nodes.statement: The polarized branch has de Rham admissibility and full pure WD comparison at every coefficient-prime place. The all-CM nonselfdual branch has de Rham admissibility, full labelled Hodge weights, ss compatibility and the monodromy upper bound of AHTW v1; spherical crystallinity and Iwahori semistability follow from WD criteria. Full N equality for general nonselfdual ramified places is not supplied by these statements. Fontaine–Laffaille, ordinary lifting and residual-image conclusions retain their separate consumer hypotheses.
proofSteps: Compare the exact outputs without upgrading a bound to equality.
Retain the branch tag on each arithmetic export.
acceptance: A ramified nonselfdual member cannot be passed to a full-WD consumer without an additional theorem.
Crystallinity at good places is sufficient for the imported weak predicate.

sources.match: Separate ss equality and N bound.
The polarized theorem identifies N.

nodes.title: Local residual genericity
nodes.statement: Let L/Q_p be any finite extension with residue cardinality q, ℓ≠p, k a finite field of characteristic ℓ, and r:G_L→GL_n(k) continuous. It is ACC+-generic at L if inertia acts trivially and, over k̄, the eigenvalues α_i∈k̄× of r(Frob_L^geom), listed with multiplicity, satisfy α_i/α_j≠q for every i≠j. Arithmetic instead of geometric Frobenius gives the same predicate because inversion reverses the ordered pair. Repeated eigenvalues are permitted when q≠1 in k; pairwise distinctness alone is insufficient. The local condition has no global irreducibility, adequacy or enormousness clause.

Split the characteristic polynomial in k̄ and test all ordered pairs of eigenvalues, retaining multiplicity.
Keep the eigenvalue predicate separate from its local representation predicate.

nodes.title: Compact Drinfeld models and Newton strata
nodes.statement: For the compact PEL datum of Shin Lemma 5.1, p split in E and distinguished w|p, construct the projective flat Drinfeld models Sh_{U^p, m-vector} over O_{F_w}. The zero distinguished level is smooth. On its geometric special fibre, Sh^(h), 0≤h≤n−1, is the locus where the one-dimensional O_{F_w}-divisible group A[w^∞] has étale height h. Equivalently its connected part has O_{F_w}-height n−h. These strata have dimension h; the locus of height at most h is closed. The remaining split factors have dimension-zero divisible groups. No unramifiedness of F_w/Q_p is imposed. The construction is restricted to this Lie-dimension-one datum; it is not a general ramified PEL integral-model theorem.
hypotheses: Shin §5.1 conditions (i)–(v), sufficiently small prime-to-p level and compatible Drinfeld levels; Lie dimension one at w and zero at the other chosen split factors.
proofSteps: Specialize the PEL integral moduli problem to the one-dimensional O_{F_w}-divisible group with determinant, polarization and level conditions.
Use Drinfeld deformation and level theory, rather than a Grothendieck–Messing argument requiring an unramified field. The precise HT01 proof remains a recorded source gap.
Stratify the reduced zero-level special fibre by étale height and preserve all prime-to-p Hecke correspondences.
acceptance: For n=3, h=2 the stratum has dimension 2 and connected O_{F_w}-height 1.
For h=0 the stratum has dimension 0 and the connected height is n.
A ramified F_w/Q_p is allowed in this datum; replacing the model by a hyperspecial unramified PEL model does not define the stated integral model.
The alternative formal-height index j is n−1−h, so its dimension n−1−j equals h.

sources.locator: §5.2, pp.32–33 (integral model and strata); Lemma 5.1, pp.30–31
sources.match: Specifies projectivity, flatness, smooth zero level and the exceptional ramified-field extension of the Drinfeld construction.

nodes.title: Compact Igusa towers before local comparison
nodes.statement: Over each compact Newton stratum Sh^(b)=Sh^(h), choose the one-dimensional O_{F_w}-divisible group Σ_b over the algebraic residue closure with the prescribed isocrystal and additional structures. In this datum its isogeny class contains one isomorphism class, so its central leaf is all Sh^(b). Construct Mantovan’s finite-level Igusa covers Ig_{b,U^p,m} and the tower, with level-transition, prime-to-p Hecke, quasi-isogeny J_b(Q_p), and descent actions on compact-support cohomology. The finite-level covers of the central leaf are smooth finite étale Galois covers as in Shin §5.2. Distinguish them from first-kind étale-part level and from perfection of an infinite-level tower. Independence of Σ_b means equivalence after an isomorphism of framing objects, not a preferred identification.
hypotheses: The compact Drinfeld datum and Newton strata; the additional structures and bounded trivializations in Mantovan’s construction.
proofSteps: Use the uniqueness of the one-dimensional framed divisible group to identify central leaf and Newton stratum.
Construct the compatible finite-level trivialization covers and their descent; retain formal as well as étale structure.
Pass to compact-support cohomology and level colimits; record the commuting quasi-isogeny and prime-to-p Hecke actions.
acceptance: A nonempty finite Igusa cover of Sh^(h) has dimension h, as finite étale maps preserve dimension.
For h=0 the finite-level covers are zero-dimensional; the tower still has level data.
Trivializing only the étale summand cannot supply the full Mantovan cover when the connected part has nontrivial level data.
For h>0 a smooth finite-level cover is not its perfection: Frobenius on local parameters need not be invertible.

nodes.statement: For the EL factors of the compact split local datum (b,μ), construct the framed Rapoport–Zink deformation spaces over O_{F_w^ur-hat}, their generic-fibre level tower M^rig_{b,μ,U_p}, and H_c^j with smooth J_b(Q_p), G(Q_p) and Weil descent actions. A point is a deformation of the framed O_{F_w}-divisible group together with the framing quasi-isogeny and rational level; the other dimension-zero factors and similitude factor are retained. The dimension D of the generic fibre is part of the normalization. This is the classical EL special case required by Shin, not a construction of arbitrary local shtukas or spectral-action machinery.
hypotheses: The compact one-dimensional EL signature and additional level structures of Shin §5.2, including ramified F_w; use the unramified-completion base of that source.
proofSteps: Apply the local deformation problem at the distinguished factor and the dimension-zero factor problems; representability and finiteness are exact requested moduli/cohomology inputs.
Equip the tower with changing-framing, level and descent actions; commute them before taking cohomology.
Use the compact-support six-functor formalism for the generic fibres, retaining the dimension and transition maps.

nodes.title: The compact Mantovan Ext functor
nodes.statement: For a finite-length smooth J_b(Q_p)-representation ρ in the admissible compact EL setting define Mant_{b,μ}([ρ]) = Σ_{i,j} (−1)^{i+j} [colim_{U_p} Ext^i_{J_b(Q_p)-smooth}(H_c^j(M^rig_{b,μ,U_p}),ρ)](−D), a Grothendieck class for G(Q_p)×W_{F_w}. Use finite/cohomologically bounded alternating sums and the commuting actions from the towers. Additivity extends it to the Grothendieck group. With prime-to-p coefficients carried along, the compact almost-product comparison yields [H(Sh,L_ξ)]=Σ_b Mant_{b,μ}([H_c(Ig_b,L_ξ)]). This identity is virtual; no individual cohomology degree or actual rank-n summand follows from it alone.
hypotheses: Smooth derived Ext with level colimits and bounded admissibility; compact almost-product/coefficient descent for this datum. These are explicit supplier contracts, not consequences of local LLC.
proofSteps: Form derived smooth Hom from the local compact-support complex into the Igusa representation and take the alternating cohomology class.
Apply the almost-product comparison on each Newton stratum and descend coefficients, retaining all actions.
Sum strata, insert (−D), and use Künneth for the split factors as in Shin (5.6). Local reduction via ET.6a is a separate application to this expression.
acceptance: A single nonzero Ext^1 of H_c^0 contributes with negative sign, unlike Ext^0 of H_c^0.
A dimension-D factor carries the twist (−D); omitting it changes geometric Frobenius eigenvalues by q^(−D).
[V]−[V]=0 in the Grothendieck group does not imply V=0 and cannot select an actual automorphic constituent.

nodes.title: The HLTT split unitary datum
nodes.statement: For CM F=F_0F^+ with F_0 imaginary quadratic and n≥1, take V=F^{2n} with skew-Hermitian form Σ_{i=1}^n(x_i conjugate(y_{2n+1−i})−x_{2n+1−i} conjugate(y_i)) and its Q-trace alternating form. Let G_n over Q be its unitary similitude group with similitude ν, and G_n^0=ker ν. At every real place the unitary signature is (n,n). An integral lattice and its trace-dual define the integral level model; no reductivity at ramified primes is inferred. For p split in F_0 use the split local factorization with GL_{2n}(F_w) and the Levi GL_1×Res_{F/Q}GL_n of the Siegel parabolic, in the source’s fixed identifications. The Shimura dimension is [F^+:Q]n². This specializes PELModuli; it does not define a second general unitary group theory.
hypotheses: HLTT §§1,3; source-compatible lattice, positivity, determinant and level conditions.
proofSteps: Specialize the generic PEL similitude construction to the hyperbolic skew-Hermitian space.
Compute the real signatures and the split local Levi; retain the similitude factor.
Import ordinary integral models and compactifications in the application node, rather than building them into the group definition.

nodes.title: Compatible-family data before admissibility
nodes.statement: Fix number fields F,M, algebraic closures and compatible embeddings used to compare labels. A rank-n compatible-family datum consists of a finite set S of finite places of F; monic degree-n polynomials P_v∈M[X] with nonzero constant term for v∉S; actual continuous semisimple representations r_λ:G_F→GL_n(algebraicClosure(M_λ)) for every finite place λ of M; and n-element multisets H_τ⊂Z for embeddings τ:F→algebraicClosure(M). Require r_λ unramified at v∉S, v∤char(k_λ), and charpoly(r_λ(Frob_v^geom)) equal to the specified image of P_v, for every compatible coefficient embedding. H_τ is metadata at this level: de Rhamness and agreement with actual labelled weights are separate predicates. Morphisms consist of the same S, polynomials and labels and memberwise equivariant isomorphisms. Enlarging S is restriction of good-place indexing, not literal equality of data. The rank-zero datum is allowed, with P_v=1, empty H and the zero-dimensional member.
hypotheses: All members are actual representations, not just traces. Coefficient embeddings and their compatibility with λ are fixed in the label comparison.
proofSteps: Assemble polynomial and representation data over the ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations carriers; transport coefficient embeddings through the fixed algebraic closures.
Impose only common good-place polynomial compatibility; attach all period, purity and polarization conditions as predicates.
Use characteristic-polynomial recognition only for memberwise uniqueness up to isomorphism.
acceptance: The cyclotomic family has n=1, S=∅, P_v=X−q_v^{-1}, H_τ={−1}; arithmetic Frobenius would give q_v instead.
Rank zero has P_v=1 and empty H_τ; a definition requiring positive rank would exclude it.
Assigning wrong H_τ to the trivial family still defines raw data, but it fails weak and determinant-Hodge compatibility.
For the cohomological Δ family at q=2, P_2=X²+24X+2048 and H={11,0}.
A scalar automorphism of an irreducible member preserves every P_v; common polynomials do not choose an intertwiner or basis.

nodes.title: Weak, very weak and extremely weak compatibility
nodes.statement: On compatible-family data define Weak: every r_λ is de Rham at every v|ℓ, its labelled HT multiset is H_τ for every compatible coefficient embedding, and it is crystalline at v|ℓ outside S. Define ExtremelyWeak: det r_λ is de Rham at every v|ℓ with labelled HT weight Σ H_τ for all λ. Define VeryWeak: ExtremelyWeak and a set of rational primes of Dirichlet density one such that for every λ above one of these primes, every v|ℓ is crystalline with the full labelled multiset H_τ. This density-one set can omit the finitely many rational characteristics below S. Then Weak implies VeryWeak implies ExtremelyWeak. Neither weakened predicate asserts admissibility of each rank-n member at every coefficient prime. Genericity or residual irreducibility is not a field of any of these predicates.
hypotheses: Use geometric Frobenius and HT(ε)=−1 throughout. Density is on rational coefficient primes and quantifies every λ above them, not one selected λ.
proofSteps: Define the determinant-Hodge condition and the independent density-one crystalline/full-weight condition.
For Weak⇒VeryWeak omit the finite set of rational primes below S and use compatibility of D_dR with determinants.
For VeryWeak⇒ExtremelyWeak forget the density-one clause; no limiting Hodge assertion is used.
acceptance: ε is weak, very weak and extremely weak, with labelled weight −1.
Rank zero satisfies all three conditions, with determinant 1 of weight zero.
In rank two H={0,2} and H′={1,1} have the same determinant weight but different full labelled multisets.
A density-one claim for one chosen λ above each ℓ is weaker than the required statement for every λ above those ℓ.

nodes.title: Operations on compatible-family data
nodes.statement: For families over the same F, first extend coefficient fields to a common number field and enlarge S to the union. Define direct sum, tensor, dual, conjugation by an automorphism c of F, restriction to a finite extension, and tensoring by an algebraic-character family on actual members and on H_τ. Direct sums concatenate H, tensor products use all pairwise sums, dual negates H and inverts polynomial roots. Good P_v are the corresponding characteristic polynomials (for a tensor product use the universal resultant expression, not multiplication of P_v). Weak, VeryWeak and ExtremelyWeak are preserved by these operations, with rational density-one intersections where needed; regularity, irreducibility and cuspidal automorphy require separate hypotheses. Restriction at w|v replaces good roots α by α^{f(w/v)}. Semisimplify members when necessary in the characteristic-zero family category and use its polynomial invariance.
hypotheses: Continuous finite-dimensional semisimple characteristic-zero member theory and common embeddings; scalar extension and tensor semisimplicity are supplied by R01.1, not by an arbitrary positive-characteristic tensor assertion.
proofSteps: Apply each functor to actual members and transport continuity; compute good polynomials universally from their roots or characteristic polynomials.
Apply the corresponding multiset operation to the H labels and prove identity/composition up to memberwise isomorphism.
Use tensor exactness of period functors and determinant formulas for the three strength predicates; retain separate conditions for the branch predicates.
acceptance: Tensoring two rank-two families gives rank four; multiplying their polynomials instead describes the direct sum.
The dual cyclotomic family has P_v=X−q_v and H={1}.
Tensor with rank zero has rank zero and P_v=1; direct sum with rank zero preserves members up to canonical isomorphism.
The rank-two trivial family tensored with itself has polynomial (X−1)^4, H={0,0,0,0}; it is neither regular nor irreducible.

nodes.title: Purity, strict compatibility and polarized families
nodes.statement: Define separate predicates on compatible-family data. Regular means every H_τ is without repetition. Pure of integral weight W means |ι(α)|²=q_v^W for every good root and every complex embedding, and H_{cτ}={W−h:h∈H_τ} when F is CM (the analogous same-embedding symmetry when F is totally real). BLGGT StrictCompatible means for every finite v a common algebraic WD parameter D_v with WD(r_λ|G_{F_v})^{F-ss}≅D_v at λ not above the residue characteristic of v. StrictPure adds WD purity of weight W for every D_v. AllPlaceStrict adds comparison at coefficient-prime places using D_pst for potentially semistable members. A polarization is a character family μ over F^+ and actual memberwise conjugate-dual identifications with the symmetry/oddness condition of G7; the pair convention is r_λ^c≅r_λ^∨⊗μ_λ. These structures are not included in raw data or Weak, and pure WD objects are owned by AG2.5 rather than redeveloped here.
hypotheses: F is CM or totally real where conjugation/polarization is invoked. Finite inertial Weil image and Frobenius semisimplification are part of each WD input.
proofSteps: Define good-root purity, labelled symmetry, and common local-parameter predicates separately.
Use the AG2.5 pure-WD interface and the G7 pairing API; no maximal-rank characterization of pure N is assumed.
Relate AllPlaceStrict to BLGGT strictness by forgetting coefficient-prime comparisons.
acceptance: ε is pure of weight −2, with H={−1}; replacing geometric q^{-1} by q would give the wrong sign of the weight.

importChecks.title: Dominant weights (ℤⁿ)^{Hom(F,Ω),+}, the subsets (ℤⁿ)_w for CM fields, base change of weights and the representations Ξ_a
importChecks.statement: For a number field F, rank n≥1 and algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field Ω, use the embedding-wise dominant GL_n coordinates of AF.4: a family a has a_{τ,1}≥⋯≥a_{τ,n} at each τ:F→Ω. The notation (ℤⁿ)^{Hom(F,Ω),+} denotes this specialization of the imported algebraic-weight carrier. For totally real or CM F with conjugation c, membership in (ℤⁿ)_w means a_{τ,i}+a_{τ∘c,n+1−i}=w for every τ and i. When Ω=ℂ, conjugating the target embedding gives the same condition. Restriction of embeddings defines base change: (a_{F′})_{τ,i}=a_{τ|_F,i}. Extreme regularity asks that, at some embedding, equal-sized subsets of the shifted entries {a_{τ,i}+n−i} are determined by their sums. For complex coefficients Ξ_a is AF.4’s highest-weight representation, identified with the tensor product of the GL_n representations of highest weights a_τ. The coordinate notation and Ξ_a do not introduce a second highest-weight theory.
hypotheses: Dominance is the ordering a_{τ,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ a_{τ,n}, with repetitions allowed; regularity of the attached Hodge–Tate numbers comes from the shift by n − i (node expected-hodge-tate-multiset), not from strictness of a.
The condition defining (ℤⁿ)_w pairs τ with τ∘c and i with n + 1 − i. It is empty unless F is totally real or CM.
Ξ_a is a representation of the complex group GL_n^{Hom(F,ℂ)} = (Res_{F/ℚ} GL_n)_ℂ. Its highest-weight theory is supplied by AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4 (algebraic highest weights).

proofSteps: Import AF.4/algebraic-weight and identify its dominant GL_n coordinates and representation V_a with the notation a and Ξ_a. Only the polarized weight-w condition and extremely-regular subset are added here.
Well-definedness: dominance and membership in (ℤⁿ)_w are finitely many linear conditions on the integers a_{τ,i}.
The two forms of the (ℤⁿ)_w condition agree for Ω = ℂ because, for F totally real or CM, τ∘c = c∘τ for every τ: F → ℂ (Mathlib's NumberField.IsCMField.complexEmbedding_complexConj).
a_{F′} is dominant, and lies in (ℤⁿ)_w for the same w when F′ is again totally real or CM and a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_w, since complex conjugation on F′ restricts to that of F.
acceptance: For integer k≥2, the classical weight-k form gives a = (k − 2, 0) at the single embedding of ℚ, which lies in (ℤ²)_{k−2}.
For F imaginary quadratic and n = 1, a = (a_τ, a_{cτ}) lies in (ℤ¹)_w with w = a_τ + a_{cτ}; w can be odd, e.g. (1, 0), the weight of the Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve.

Dominant algebraic GL_n weights allow negative integers. The polarized determinant pair has tuples (1,…,1) and (−1,…,−1), with w=0; imposing nonnegative coordinates as in CH’s misprint E7 would wrongly exclude it.

importChecks.title: Regular algebraic automorphic representations of GL_n(𝔸_F) and their weight
importChecks.statement: For an automorphic GL_n(𝔸_F) representation π over a number field F, regular algebraicity means that its archimedean infinitesimal character comes from an irreducible algebraic representation of Res_{F/ℚ} GL_n. Write its weight as the unique dominant family a for which infChar(π_∞)=infChar(Ξ_a^∨). If an algebraic Hecke character ψ has identity-component infinity type ∏_τ τ(x)^{−b_τ}, tensoring π with ψ∘det changes a_{τ,i} to a_{τ,i}+b_τ. Thus an integer norm twist π⊗‖det‖^t changes every coordinate to a_{τ,i}−t.
hypotheses: The infinitesimal character is compared with that of Ξ_a^∨, not Ξ_a; this is the convention of both BLGGT and ACC+.

Regular algebraic is Clozel's C-algebraic for GL_n. It differs from L-algebraic by the twist ‖det‖^{(n−1)/2} when n is even. The C/L distinction is owned by AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4 and is not re-planned here.
No cuspidality, self-duality or unitarity is part of the definition.

proofSteps: Well-definedness of the weight: the infinitesimal character of Ξ_a^∨ is the W-orbit of −w₀a + ρ at each τ, and these orbits determine a (AF.4's Harish-Chandra parametrisation).

Twisting: the infinitesimal character of π_∞ ⊗ (ψ_∞∘det) is that of π_∞ shifted by the exponents of ψ_∞, and Ξ_a^∨ ⊗ ∏_τ τ(det)^{−b_τ} = Ξ_{a+b}^∨. For ψ = ‖·‖^t, the identity-component exponents are b_τ = −t, since ‖x‖ = ∏_τ |τ(x)| on (F_∞^×)⁰.

importChecks.title: Conjugate self-dual, essentially conjugate self-dual and polarized automorphic representations, with the multiplier character
importChecks.statement: Let F be totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F⁺ and complex conjugation c, and π an automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F). (i) π is conjugate self-dual if π^c ≅ π^∨. (ii) π is essentially conjugate self-dual with multiplier χ if χ: 𝔸_{F⁺}^×/(F⁺)^× → ℂ^× is continuous and π^c ≅ π^∨ ⊗ (χ ∘ N_{F/F⁺} ∘ det). (iii) (π, χ) is a polarized automorphic representation if moreover χ_v(−1) is independent of v | ∞. (iv) π is polarizable if some (π, χ) is polarized. (v) A regular algebraic polarized (π, χ) of weight a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_w with F imaginary is totally odd if χ_v(−1) = (−1)^{n+w} for all v | ∞. Here π^c = π ∘ c on GL_n(𝔸_F), and π^c = π when F is totally real.
hypotheses: The multiplier χ is part of the data. It is determined by π only up to δ_{F/F⁺}, since δ_{F/F⁺} ∘ N_{F/F⁺} = 1.

BLGGT impose instead χ_v(−1) = (−1)^n for F imaginary (printed with µ in place of χ). That is the correct normalisation only when w is even; with odd w it makes the Galois multiplier even (sourceIssue AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII/E2; node sign-of-the-polarization-multiplier). Condition (v) is the corrected form, and like BLGGT's it can always be achieved by replacing χ by χδ_{F/F⁺}.
For regular algebraic (π, χ) of weight a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_w, χ is algebraic with |χ| = ‖·‖^{−w}. Conjugate self-duality is the case χ = 1, possible only when w = 0.
For F totally real, polarized means essentially self-dual with χ_v(−1) independent of v. Patrikis shows the independence is automatic for regular algebraic cuspidal π; this packet does not use that.

api.name: TauCeti.AutomorphicGalois.IsConjSelfDual

api.name: TauCeti.AutomorphicGalois.IsEssConjSelfDual
api.statement: π.IsEssConjSelfDual χ :⇔ π^c ≅ π^∨ ⊗ (χ ∘ N ∘ det).

api.name: TauCeti.AutomorphicGalois.PolarizedAutRep

api.name: TauCeti.AutomorphicGalois.PolarizedAutRep.exists_totallyOdd
api.statement: Exactly one of (π, χ), (π, χδ_{F/F⁺}) is totally odd when F is imaginary.

tests.name: TauCeti.AutomorphicGalois.not_totallyOdd_blggt_sign_odd_w
tests.statement: A pair satisfying BLGGT's printed χ_v(−1) = (−1)^n with w odd (the CM elliptic curve character) is not totally odd: its Galois multiplier takes c_v to +1.

proofSteps: Well-definedness: π^c and π^∨ ⊗ (χ ∘ N ∘ det) are automorphic representations, so the condition is an isomorphism class condition; χ_v(−1) makes sense since −1 ∈ (F⁺_v)^× at every real place v.

Weight constraint: comparing the infinitesimal characters of π^c (weight (a_{τc,i})) and π^∨ ⊗ (χ∘N∘det) (weight (−a_{τ,n+1−i} + b)), where χ has parallel exponent b, gives a_{τc,i} + a_{τ,n+1−i} = b. So a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_b and w = b, and |χ| = ‖·‖^{−w}.
Normalisation: χ and χδ_{F/F⁺} give the same condition (ii), and δ_{F/F⁺,v}(−1) = −1 at every real place v when F is imaginary. So exactly one of them satisfies (v).
acceptance: n = 1, F imaginary quadratic, ψ the Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve (weight (1, 0), w = 1): ψψ^c = ψ|_{𝔸_{F⁺}} ∘ N, and (ψ, ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ}) satisfies BLGGT's printed condition while (ψ, ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ} δ) is totally odd.

Base change of a weight-k newform to an imaginary quadratic field: π^c ≅ π and π^∨ ≅ π ⊗ ω_π^{−1}, so π is essentially conjugate self-dual with multiplier the central character of the form (twisted as needed), and w = k − 2.

importChecks.title: BLGGT pairing conventions for the imported polarized carrier
importChecks.statement: Use the continuous representation and polarized-extension carriers of R01.1 and G7. For CM F, the BLGGT pairing has symmetry ε_v=−μ(c_v), so total oddness is ε_v=1, equivalently μ(c_v)=−1; this is the convention bridge to the G_n-valued extension with multiplier μ. For totally real F, an invariant alternating (respectively symmetric) pairing has μ(c_v)=−ε_v (respectively ε_v) in the corresponding symplectic (respectively orthogonal) extension convention. Algebraic and regular conditions import the p-adic Hodge carrier, with HT(ε_ℓ)={−1}. This node specializes those carriers and does not construct a second deformation theory.
hypotheses: The condition at one infinite place implies it at all of them, with ε_{v′} = µ(c_v c_{v′})ε_v and ⟨x, y⟩_{v′} = ⟨x, r(c_v c_{v′}) y⟩_v.

For F imaginary, (r, µ) is polarized if and only if r extends to r̃: G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(Q̄_l) with multiplier µ, where 𝒢_n is the group of Clozel–Harris–Taylor (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group).
For F totally real, (r, µ) is polarized if and only if r factors through GSp_n (µ(c_v) = −ε_v) or GO_n (µ(c_v) = ε_v) with multiplier µ.
Hodge–Tate numbers use BLGGT's convention HT_τ(ε_l) = {−1}.
proofSteps: Well-definedness: the pairing condition is a closed condition on (r, µ), and the change of place v ↦ v′ is the computation quoted in the hypotheses.

Equivalence with 𝒢_n-valued extensions (F imaginary), BLGGT's second remark in §2.1: r̃(c_v) = (A, a)·j, where A is determined by the Gram matrix of ⟨ , ⟩_v and ν(r̃(c_v)) = −a = µ(c_v), so a = ε_v. Conversely, a pairing is read off from r̃(c_v). (For n = 1, r̃(c)² = 1 forces a = 1, i.e. µ(c) = −1.)
acceptance: n = 1, F imaginary: a character r with r^c = r^{−1}µ|_{G_F} is polarized with multiplier µ if and only if µ(c_v) = −1, since a non-degenerate pairing on a line is symmetric (ε_v = 1).
n = 2, F imaginary quadratic, r = ρ|_{G_F} for an odd ρ: G_ℚ → GL_2(Q̄_l): (r, det ρ) is totally odd, via the pairing ⟨x, y⟩ = det(x, ρ(c)y).

importChecks.title: The l-adic character r_{l,ι}(χ) of an algebraic Hecke character, its Hodge–Tate numbers and its weight
importChecks.statement: Let F be a number field, l a prime and ι: Q̄_l ≅ ℂ, with Art_F normalised to send uniformisers to geometric Frobenius elements. Let χ: 𝔸_F^×/F^× → ℂ^× be algebraic: χ|_{(F_∞^×)⁰}(x) = ∏_{τ ∈ Hom(F,ℂ)} τ(x)^{−a_τ} with a_τ ∈ ℤ. There is a unique continuous character r_{l,ι}(χ): G_F → Q̄_l^× with ι ∘ r_{l,ι}(χ)|_{W_{F_v}} ∘ Art_{F_v} = χ_v for all v ∤ l; explicitly ι((r_{l,ι}(χ) ∘ Art_F)(x) ∏_τ (ι^{−1}τ)(x_l)^{a_τ}) = χ(x) ∏_τ (τ x_∞)^{a_τ}. It is de Rham above l with HT_τ(r_{l,ι}(χ)) = {a_{ι∘τ}}. The weight wt(χ) is the integer with |χ| = ‖·‖^{−wt(χ)/2}. Then a_τ + a_{τ′} = wt(χ) whenever τ|_{F₀} = τ′|_{F₀} ∘ c (F₀ the maximal CM subfield), wt(χ) is even when F₀ is totally real, wt(‖·‖_F) = −2, r_{l,ι}(‖·‖) = ε_l, and r_{l,ι}(χ)(c_v) = χ_v(−1)(−1)^{wt(χ)/2} at every real place v when F is totally real.
hypotheses: The normalisation of Art_F (uniformisers ↦ geometric Frobenius) fixes r_{l,ι}(‖·‖) = ε_l. With the arithmetic normalisation it would be ε_l^{−1}.
HT_τ(ε_l) = {−1} in this convention, consistent with HT_τ(r_{l,ι}(χ)) = {a_{ι∘τ}} and a = −1 for ‖·‖ over ℚ.
The value at complex conjugation is computed at real places only: at a complex place there is no c_v in G_F.

tests.statement: For F imaginary and ψ algebraic on F, r_{l,ι}(ψ|_{𝔸_{F⁺}})(c_v) = +1 because the transfer sends c_v to c_v² = 1, whatever ψ_v(−1) is: the Galois sign is not χ_v(−1) unless wt/2 is even.

proofSteps: The displayed formula defines a continuous character of 𝔸_F^×/F^×(F_∞^×)⁰ with values in Q̄_l^× (the correction factor at l cancels χ_∞ on F^×). Global Artin reciprocity (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory, layer 11) turns it into r_{l,ι}(χ).
Local compatibility at v ∤ l is immediate from the formula. Uniqueness follows from Čebotarev density of the unramified Frobenius elements.
Hodge–Tate numbers: on an open subgroup of O_{F_v}^× (v | l), r ∘ Art is ∏_τ τ^{−a_τ}, a Lubin–Tate character product, whose τ-Hodge–Tate number is a_{ι∘τ} (Serre, Abelian l-adic representations).
Weight: |χ| = ‖·‖^{−wt/2} and the unit theorem give a_τ + a_{τ′} = wt for conjugate pairs; for F₀ totally real all a_τ are equal, so wt = 2a is even.
Value at c_v for F totally real: χ = χ₀‖·‖^{−wt/2} with χ₀ of finite order. Then r(χ) = r(χ₀)ε_l^{−wt/2}, r(χ₀)(c_v) = χ_{0,v}(−1) = χ_v(−1) because Art_ℝ(−1) = c, and ε_l(c_v) = −1.
acceptance: F = ℚ, χ = ‖·‖: r = ε_l and HT = {−1}, i.e. a = −1 and wt = −2.

F = ℚ, ω of finite order and unramified at p ∤ l: r_{l,ι}(ω)(Frob_p) = ω_p(p) for the geometric Frobenius, so the arithmetic Frobenius goes to ω_p(p)^{−1}. Which of χ(p)^{±1} this is for a Dirichlet character χ depends on how χ is made idelic, and must be fixed once (GlobalNumberFields layer 9's Dirichlet dictionary).
The Hecke character ψ of a CM elliptic curve E over its CM field K (weight (1, 0)): r_{l,ι}(ψ) ⊕ r_{l,ι}(ψ^c) is the restriction to G_K of the dual of V_l(E), in this convention.

importChecks.title: The parity of the Galois multiplier of a polarized pair: µ(c_v) = (−1)^{n−1+w} χ_v(−1)
importChecks.statement: Let F be imaginary CM and (π, χ) a regular algebraic polarized automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_w. Put µ = ε_l^{1−n} r_{l,ι}(χ): G_{F⁺} → Q̄_l^×. Then µ(c_v) = (−1)^{n−1+w} χ_v(−1) for every v | ∞. Hence µ is totally odd if and only if χ_v(−1) = (−1)^{n+w}, i.e. (π, χ) is totally odd in the sense of polarized-automorphic-representation (v). Under BLGGT's printed normalisation χ_v(−1) = (−1)^n, µ(c_v) = (−1)^{w+1}: it is −1 exactly when w is even.
hypotheses: The integer w is the one with a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_w. Theorem 2.1.1 of BLGGT uses a different integer, the purity weight w + n − 1 of r_{l,ι}(π).
Only the multiplier's value at complex conjugation is computed. No Galois representation r_{l,ι}(π) is needed for the statement.
proofSteps: By polarized-automorphic-representation, χ is algebraic with parallel exponent b = w on 𝔸_{F⁺}, so wt(χ) = 2w.
By galois-character-of-an-algebraic-hecke-character, r_{l,ι}(χ)(c_v) = χ_v(−1)(−1)^w.

Consequence for BLGGT Theorem 2.1.1(1): the pair (r_{l,ι}(π), ε_l^{1−n} r_{l,ι}(χ)) is totally odd only for the multiplier χ satisfying (v). With χ_v(−1) = (−1)^n and w odd, µ(c_v) = +1, and (r_{l,ι}(π), µ) is not even polarized for n = 1 (a pairing on a line is symmetric).
Independent check against Patrikis, who records the sign of the pairing preserved by these representations as ω_ι(c_v) = (−1)^w ω_v(−1) in his normalisation.
acceptance: n = 1, F = K imaginary quadratic, ψ the Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve (weight (1, 0), w = 1): ψψ^c = ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ} ∘ N. χ = ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ} has χ_∞(−1) = (−1)^1 = −1, BLGGT's sign. But r_{l,ι}(ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ})(c) = 1 (transfer), whereas χ = ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ}δ_K, with χ_∞(−1) = +1 = (−1)^{n+w}, gives µ(c) = −1.

n = 2, the base change to K of a newform of weight k with k odd (w = k − 2 odd): BLGGT's sign gives µ(c) = +1. The invariant pairing on r = ρ_f^∨|_{G_K} is symmetric (det(x, ρ(c)y)), so the totally odd multiplier is the other one, the extension of det r with value −1 at c.
w even (for instance n = 1 and ψ with ψψ^c = 1): the corrected and printed normalisations agree.

importChecks.title: The Hodge–Tate multiset attached to a weight: HT_τ = {a_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, …, a_{ιτ,n}}
importChecks.statement: For a ∈ (ℤⁿ)^{Hom(F,ℂ),+}, ι: Q̄_l ≅ ℂ and τ: F → Q̄_l, put HT_τ(a) = {a_{ι∘τ,i} + n − i : 1 ≤ i ≤ n}, a multiset of n integers, in BLGGT's convention HT_τ(ε_l) = {−1}. The elements are distinct, so a Galois representation with these Hodge–Tate numbers is regular. If F is CM and a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_w, then HT_{τ∘c}(a) = {w + n − 1 − h : h ∈ HT_τ(a)}. Twisting a by −t (π ↦ π ⊗ ‖det‖^t) subtracts t from every element, matching ⊗ ε_l^t. In the opposite convention (HT(ε_l) = +1) every element is negated.
hypotheses: This is the target that AG2.6 proves for r_{l,ι}(π) (BLGGT Theorem 2.1.1(3), ACC+ Theorem 2.3.3(b)); here it is only the dictionary from a to a multiset.
The integer w + n − 1 is BLGGT's w in Theorem 2.1.1(3). The two integers must not be confused.

importChecks.title: Automorphic specialization of the integral Hecke polynomial
importChecks.statement: Let v be a finite place of F with q_v = #k(v), π_v an unramified irreducible representation of GL_n(F_v), and t_{v,i} the eigenvalue on π_v^{GL_n(O_{F_v})} of T_{v,i} = [GL_n(O_{F_v}) diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) GL_n(O_{F_v})] (ϖ_v repeated i times). Define P_v(π_v; X) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} t_{v,i} X^{n−i}. If α₁, …, α_n are the Satake parameters of π_v, with t_{v,i} = q_v^{i(n−i)/2} e_i(α), then P_v(π_v; X) = ∏_j (X − q_v^{(n−1)/2} α_j). Conventions: a Galois representation r corresponds to π at v in the geometric convention (BLGGT, ACC+, HLTT: Frob_v geometric, Art uniformisers ↦ geometric Frobenius) if ι det(X − r(Frob_v)) = P_v(π_v; X). It corresponds in the arithmetic convention (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3, and R19) if the arithmetic Frobenius has characteristic polynomial P_v(π_v; X). r corresponds in one convention if and only if r^∨ corresponds in the other. Twists: P_v(π_v ⊗ ‖det‖^t; X) = q_v^{−tn} P_v(π_v; q_v^t X), matching r ↦ r ⊗ ε_l^t. The contragredient has roots q_v^{n−1}/β_j, where β_j are the roots for π_v, matching r ↦ r^∨ ⊗ ε_l^{1−n}.
hypotheses: No local Langlands correspondence is used. For unramified π_v, 'r corresponds at v' is defined by the polynomial identity, which is what AG2.0 requires. Agreement with rec(π_v ⊗ |det|^{(1−n)/2}) for unramified π_v is an AG2.5 comparison.

ACC+ say P_v corresponds to Frobenius on rec^T(π_v), their arithmetic normalisation of local Langlands (Clozel–Thorne §2.1), with Frob_v geometric in their notation. That is the geometric convention here.
proofSteps: Import the normalized Satake and integral polynomial declarations from IHG.3; specialize the coefficient ring along the spherical Hecke eigencharacter of π_v.
Use the imported scalar-twist and reciprocal-polynomial identities, with ε_ℓ(Frob_geom)=q_v^(−1), to obtain norm, contragredient and Frobenius conversion formulas.
For rank two compare the resulting polynomial with the classical Hecke eigenvalues; this is a polynomial acceptance check and does not use a modular Galois existence theorem.
acceptance: n = 1: P_v(X) = X − χ_v(ϖ_v), and r_{l,ι}(χ)(Frob_v) = ι^{−1}χ_v(ϖ_v) in the geometric convention (galois-character-of-an-algebraic-hecke-character).

n = 2, F = ℚ, π = π_f ⊗ ‖det‖^{1−k/2}, normalised so that T_{p,1} acts by a_p and T_{p,2} by ψ(p)p^{k−2}: P_p(X) = X² − a_pX + ψ(p)p^{k−1}. This is the R19 polynomial of ρ_f for arithmetic Frobenius, so the geometric convention gives r_{l,ι}(π) ≅ ρ_f^∨. For Δ at p = 2: X² + 24X + 2^{11}.
n = 3: P_v(X) = X³ − t₁X² + q t₂X − q³ t₃ = ∏(X − qα_j) when t₁ = q e₁, t₂ = q e₂ and t₃ = e₃.

sources.match: Use all signed coefficients of the characteristic polynomial. The terminal sign and unitary powers in the displayed definitions require the corrections recorded as E6; the packet’s GL_n polynomial already has the correct signs and degrees.
The geometric convention in the construction HLTT–ACC+ use (Frob_v geometric).

importChecks.title: A Galois representation attached to π at the good places, and its functoriality under twist, dual, conjugation and base change
importChecks.statement: For regular algebraic cuspidal π, a coefficient isomorphism ι:Q̄_ℓ≅C, and a continuous semisimple rank-n representation r of G_F unramified outside a finite set, IsAttached(ι,r,π) means that outside a finite set of finite places v∤ℓ, π_v is spherical, r is unramified, and ι det(X−r(Frob_v^geom))=P_v(π_v;X). The exceptional set contains the ramification of π, F and r and the coefficient prime. Two such r are isomorphic by Frobenius density. This is a good-place condition; it asserts neither local Langlands compatibility at ramified places nor de Rham admissibility nor global existence.
hypotheses: This is the property HLTT prove for every regular algebraic cuspidal π over a CM field (ACC+ Theorem 2.3.2). It is the interface that AG2.1–AG2.4 produce and AG2.5 strengthens. Nothing at the places in S, or above l, is asserted.
Uniqueness needs semisimplicity. It uses Čebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1/R01.5).

The base-change clause needs the Satake parameters of BC(π)_w to be the q-power restrictions of those of π_v (the unramified base-change identity), requested from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7, which exports the Arthur–Clozel base-change steps to this roadmap.

importChecks.title: Rationality of the good Hecke polynomials
importChecks.statement: Import M_π=C^{Aut(C/π^∞)} and Clozel rationality from AF.4. For regular algebraic cuspidal π on GL_n over a CM or totally real field, every spherical integral Hecke polynomial P_v(π_v;X) has coefficients in M_π. At good places the traces of any attached r therefore lie in ι^(−1)(M_π). This controls traces, not a model of r over (M_π)_λ: the Schur-index obstruction is supplied by R01.5. Coefficient conjugation sends M_π to M_{σπ}=σ(M_π).
hypotheses: The definition uses π^∞ only. σπ^∞ is π^∞ with scalars extended along σ.

M_π controls traces, not realizations. The field over which r can be written may be strictly larger, by a Schur-index obstruction. AG2.3/finite-number-field-of-realization proves a common realization field using the regular labelled Hodge–Tate input supplied by AG2.6; the early rationality theorem does not depend on that late result.
Clozel's theorem is used with its exact hypotheses: π regular algebraic (cohomological) and cuspidal. It is not claimed for non-cuspidal or non-algebraic π.
proofSteps: The spherical Hecke algebra and its integral normalization are defined over Q, so t_{v,i}(σπ)=σ(t_{v,i}(π)).
The rational factors q_v^(i(i−1)/2) are fixed by Aut(C); take invariants under the stabilizer of π^∞.
Use AF.4 for finiteness of M_π and R01.5 for the distinction between a trace field and a realization field.
acceptance: n = 1: M_ψ is the field generated by the values of ψ on 𝔸_F^{∞,×}, a number field for algebraic ψ.

n = 2: for π = π_f ⊗ ‖det‖^{1−k/2}, M_π = ℚ(a_p, ψ(p) : p ∤ N) = K_f, the Hecke field, and ρ_{f,λ} is realised over K_{f,λ} (Deligne–Serre footnote (2): complex conjugation has distinct rational eigenvalues).

Realisation is a separate question: the two-dimensional representation of the quaternion group Q₈ has rational character but is not realisable over ℚ₂, since the quaternion algebra (−1, −1)_ℚ ramifies at 2. So an Artin representation of G_ℚ through a Q₈-extension has trace field ℚ but no model over ℚ₂.

importChecks.title: Strong coefficient field
importChecks.statement: For Π regular cohomological cuspidal conjugate-self-dual (including Liu’s relevant specialization with archimedean principal series arg^{1−n},arg^{3−n},…,arg^{n−1}) and a number field E⊂C containing Q(Π), E is a strong coefficient field if for each finite λ of E there exists a continuous E_λ-linear ρ_{Π,λ} whose scalar extension to Q̄_ℓ is ρ_{Π,ι} for every ι inducing λ. Members are unique up to E_λ-conjugacy when descended by the semisimple realization theorem. This is a field of definition of the representations, stronger than the field of rationality of good polynomials. It includes a family of descended realizations, not canonical bases or canonical intertwiners. This generalizes Liu’s named definition beyond its relevant specialization, using the simultaneous realization condition justified by Chenevier–Harris Proposition 3.2.5; Liu’s conditional minimal-field assertion remains confined to his specialization and Hypothesis 3.2.10.

Use descent/uniqueness only after scalar extension; record E_λ-linear conjugacy as the equivalence relation.

importChecks.title: Rank-two compatible-family comparison
importChecks.statement: Given an independently supplied family of continuous semisimple rank-two representations of the same regular classical or Hilbert eigenform, compare each coefficient-prime member with the AG2 family by the AG2.5 memberwise comparison. Hilbert parity and half-integer normalization remain those of the independent theorem. importChecks.title: Residual genericity outside finitely many λ
importChecks.statement: For a relevant Π with a strong coefficient field E in Liu et al., choose the regular unramified place used in Chenevier–Harris’s argument, with distinct algebraic Satake roots α_i and α_i≠qα_j. After a finite extension of E containing these roots, exclude the finitely many coefficient places dividing denominators, roots, α_i−α_j or α_i−qα_j. Their reductions are distinct and nonratio. Liu Appendix D, Corollary D.1.4 then uses Chebotarev to obtain a place w split in F/F⁺ that is locally generic for the reduced Hecke eigencharacter outside this finite set. The cohomological concentration conclusion has its own F^+≠Q and level hypotheses and belongs to the Igusa/torsion consumer. This conclusion does not itself provide the completely split rational prime, generic at every v above it, required by the ACC+ global predicate; that stronger witness needs its separate Chebotarev hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the relevant polarized regular representation and a regular unramified Frobenius from CH.
Local genericity of the characteristic-zero π excludes the q-ratios.
Exclude finitely many algebraic bad factors and use the Appendix D split-place Chebotarev argument.
Pass the resulting generic Hecke ideal to the consumer rather than importing concentration back into AG2.6.
acceptance: A nonzero algebraic difference can vanish at finitely many λ; these λ must be excluded.
No absolute residual irreducibility or enormousness follows from this local condition.

importChecks.title: Unitary discrete-parameter export
importChecks.statement: In the compact unitary setting of CS Corollary 5.5.5, export the semisimple representation r_{Π^S,ℓ}=⊕_{i=1}^2 r_i⊗ε_i attached to an endoscopic discrete parameter of ranks n_1+n_2=n, with each ε_i the algebraic character of |det|^{(n_i−n)/2}·(ϖ∘N_{F/𝒦}∘det)^{ε(n−n_i)}, and ε(m)≡m mod 2. The polynomial at every v over q∈Spl_{𝒦/Q} outside S∪{ℓ} is the explicit degree-n Hecke polynomial. Keep the constituent labels, algebraic twist maps, and the away-ℓ local comparison from Remark 5.5.6. This package need not be globally irreducible and carries no coefficient-prime comparison beyond what its constituents separately prove. Here F=F⁺·𝒦 with 𝒦 the imaginary quadratic field of CS §5.1; the printed F₀ in Corollary 5.5.5 is the already confirmed E11 misprint, not another splitting field.
hypotheses: For the literal CS Corollary 5.5.5 application, retain the §5.1 unitary datum and the given irreducible admissible Π^S in the indicated BCS supercuspidal alternating Igusa summand. Its identification with the labelled pure automorphic transfer parameter is supplied as input; this export does not prove an Igusa trace or concentration theorem.

The constituent Π_i are regular C-algebraic, θ-stable isobaric representations supplied by that parameter, and r_i has rank n_i (known E10), not n. The source setup has F⁺≠Q, quasi-split finite unitary group, and the ramified rational primes of F contained in Spl_{F/F⁺}; these source restrictions are retained for that literal application.
ϖ:𝔸_𝒦×/𝒦×→ℂ× is the specified auxiliary character with odd infinity exponent; the norm is its argument, not a substitute for this character.
proofSteps: Use the ET.7a pure stable/endoscopic transfer and the AG2.2 constituent representations.
Install ε_i with the parity correction so the indicated twist is L-algebraic.
Take the direct sum and match normalized Satake polynomials using local LLC compatibility away from ℓ.
acceptance: The two-constituent sum is allowed to be reducible.
Theorem 5.5.4’s finite-place statement is used only at v∤ℓ, correcting the known E83 extraction finding.
The known E10/E11 corrections are respected: constituent rank n_i and q split in 𝒦, not an undefined F₀.

importChecks.title: Rank-two residual comparison with R19
importChecks.statement: For the regular classical/Hilbert overlap, suppose an independent rank-two realization with the normalized good polynomials has been supplied. Fix λ and the characteristic-zero dual/twist identification of AG2.6. This is a conditional comparison on semisimple classes, not a preferred lattice or an import of R19 existence or geometry. The higher-tier R19 consumer may apply it to its constructed realization.

Choose stable lattices and use residual semisimple independence, compatibility with duals and integral twists, to compare reductions.
Compare normalized reduced Hecke eigencharacters and their kernels.

requests.need:
Infinitesimal characters for the archimedean (g,K)-modules of Res GL_n, including restriction to the connected real subgroup.
Discrete compact-quotient automorphic decomposition with fixed central character and its comparison to (g,K)-cohomology; enough to identify multiplicity spaces at finite level.

Shin Proposition 5.3(i): the exact cohomological archimedean packet, its Lie-algebra cohomology degree/dimensions and highest-weight partition, needed before Corollary 6.5(iv) can identify the selected multiplicities.

The de Rham and Hodge–Tate conditions on a continuous representation, with labelled Hodge–Tate multiset and HT(ε_ℓ)={−1}; used only to interpret BLGGT terminology, not to prove automorphic admissibility.
Serre regular-Hodge–Tate algebraic-monodromy criterion: distinct labelled weights force a regular-semisimple element of the Zariski closure, as used in CH Proposition 3.2.5. Automorphic de Rham and labelled regularity proofs are the AG2.6 output.

Berger–Colmez bounded constant-Hodge-type family theorem in the CH Theorem 2.3 setting, at coefficient-prime places other than the weight-varying v_0; prove strict period comparison on that family. This is a family extension of the scalar period-functor API, not a claim that de Rham representations are closed under arbitrary limits.

Labelled D_dR and HT comparisons commute with determinant, tensor, dual, restriction and coefficient change; HT(ε)=−1 at the AG2 boundary. For fixed bounded weights on reduced rigid affinoids, period-admissibility closedness applies after a proper representation-realization cover and stable lattice/blowup, including reducible fibres (Chenevier pp.22–24).
Geometric Artin reciprocity on the idele class group modulo the connected archimedean component; compatibility with local Artin maps and transfer for extension of number fields.

Idele Hecke characters, local components and finite-order parity, including the conductor-compatible Dirichlet dictionary.
Prime-degree Grunwald–Wang theorem with totally real local conditions, S-splitting and linear disjointness from arbitrary M; this is an extension of the global-field direction and must be owned there, as a proposed Part II if the upstream layers do not cover it.

TY §2 realization L_ξ=ε_ξ R^{m_ξ}(A_U^{m_ξ}/X_U)(t_ξ), including explicit ξ↦(m_ξ,t_ξ,ε_ξ), central character and graded permutation signs.

Banach spaces of overconvergent definite-unitary automorphic forms with compact v₀ controlling operator, the fixed other infinity weights and linked tame-level maps. L2a only glues supplied families.
Definite-unitary classicality at sufficiently dominant varied weights relative to a finite slope, and Zariski density of slightly regular classical points with the other weights fixed, as in CH Theorem 2.3 / Ch Theorems 3.3 and 3.5.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.1, p. 32 (sign normalisation) and Theorem 2.1.1(1) with its proof, pp. 33–34; published Annals pp. 536–538
sourceIssues.printed: The CM automorphic sign condition is independent of w, namely χ_v(−1)=(−1)^n after repairing the symbol. Theorem 2.1.1(1) then asserts total oddness for the multiplier ε_l^{1−n}r_{l,ι}(χ), and the proof evaluates it at complex conjugation as −1.
sourceIssues.correction: For F imaginary and (π, χ) regular algebraic of weight a ∈ (ℤⁿ)_w, the normalisation making (r_{l,ι}(π), ε_l^{1−n} r_{l,ι}(χ)) totally odd is χ_v(−1) = (−1)^{n+w}. Equivalently, ε_l^{1−n} r_{l,ι}(χ)(c_v) = (−1)^{n−1+w} χ_v(−1), so the printed (−1)^n is right exactly when w is even. The stated result affected is Theorem 2.1.1(1) for odd w; the theorem holds for every polarizable π after replacing χ by χδ_{F/F⁺}, so no result about polarizable π is lost.
sourceIssues.reason: χ is algebraic on the totally real F⁺ with wt(χ) = 2w (compare infinitesimal characters in π^c ≅ π^∨ ⊗ χ∘N∘det). By BLGGT A.2, r_{l,ι}(χ) = r_{l,ι}(χ₀) ε_l^{−w} with χ₀ of finite order, so r_{l,ι}(χ)(c_v) = (−1)^w χ_v(−1), and µ(c_v) = (−1)^{n−1+w} χ_v(−1). Counterexample for w odd: n = 1, F imaginary quadratic, ψ the Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve (weight (1, 0)). (ψ, ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ}) satisfies the printed conditions, since ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ} has sign (−1)^1 at ∞. But r_{l,ι}(ψ|_{𝔸_ℚ}) = r_{l,ι}(ψ)∘V (V the transfer) takes c to r_{l,ι}(ψ)(c²) = 1, so µ(c) = +1. A pairing on a line is symmetric, so (r_{l,ι}(ψ), µ) is not polarized, let alone totally odd. The same happens for the base change of a newform of odd weight k (w = k − 2). Patrikis (Math. Ann. 362, p. 8 of arXiv v2) gives the general sign as ω_ι(c_v) = (−1)^w ω_v(−1), consistent with this correction.

sourceIssues.reason: For q=4, fix an unramified semisimple Weil representation whose geometric Frobenius is diag(8,2,2,1/2,1/2,1/8), with weights (3,1,1,−1,−1,−3). Let N_p have chains (0,1,3,5),(2,4), and N_i have chains (0,1,3),(2,4,5), each sending an entry to the next. Both satisfy FNF^−1=N/4 and have rank 4, the maximum allowed by the graded dimensions (1,2,2,1). N_p is pure of weight 0 with strings of lengths 4 and 2. N_i has strings of length 3 centred at weights 1 and −1, is not pure, and has N_i³=0 while rank N_p³=1. Thus the maximizing WD class is not unique even up to equivalence. Literal uniqueness of a matrix N must also be replaced by equivalence.

The historical normalization id belongs to AG2.5 and the historical polarized-input milestone belongs to AG2.3. The CS arbitrary-regular discrete specialization belongs after interpolation in AG2.3; the simultaneous realization-field theorem belongs after period admissibility in AG2.6. Retain all four historical ids and apply parentReconciliation, avoiding artificial layer cycles.

restructure.proposal: Move the compact Drinfeld/Igusa, classical EL cohomology/Mantovan, HLTT datum, and common compatible-family data/strength/purity/operations to the new nodes of this packet. Redirect old consumer edges using dependencyReconciliation. Later R24, R19 and IG import these owners. R19 comparisons here are conditional recognition of an independently supplied representation and import no R19 existence or Skinner theorem.

Its regular GL4 input is this roadmap’s polarized comparison. completion.closure: Complete target-level pass: all ten stages are planned (AG2.1 is a process aggregate), every target chain ends in the pinned libraries, a named supplier or a recorded gap, and the specified graph and its layer contraction are acyclic. Revision 2 recorded the installation of the importChecks contracts as a blocked integration step; REV-AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII~2 accepted the specification and records that installation, with the six external redirects, as an action for the maintainer (gap 18). No stage is closed or implemented.

review.notes: Independent review of revision 2 (issue #10008), Claude session claude-4kbXWw. All 124 effective contracts (16 nodes, 108 importChecks) were read in full, and every source locator was located in the identified versions, 26 recorded sources plus the published Caraiani author copy; all hashes match. All 15 pinned Mathlib declarations were read at 082e2d3. Prerequisites all resolve, none cites a higher tier, and the target graph and its layer contraction are acyclic. All 16 source issues are confirmed and one CH misprint is added (EAG27-1). Corrections: Shin’s and Caraiani’s L_n applies rec to the contragredient, so their R_l(Π) is attached in the AG2.0 sense to Π^∨ (dictionary node and two proof steps); Caraiani’s cited “Proposition 5.8” is Lemma 5.7 and Theorem 5.8 in arXiv v1 (two contracts and request 20); a source record for the published Caraiani author copy; and locators or matches in 16 further contracts. The suggested Lean file now uses the packet’s API names and elaborates with placeholder-proof warnings only. Status set to complete: every stage is planned. Gap 18 is an installation action for the maintainer, not a mathematical gap: importChecks, parent moves, five exclusions and six external redirects must be applied over the historical parts, which the merger does not do by itself; the specification is accepted with that action recorded.
